author: ojiudezue
title: Zone-1 manual strands are URA trusting a status-lagged Carrier 'manual' after a borrow returns — not the Bryant schedule, and URA was wrongly exonerated
summary: Attribution of 88 zone_1 manual entries after the 09-20 schedule removal: ~70 were URA's own AC nudge borrows (start/restore), but those last 2-5 min and always return; the 24.9 h of strand time is 4 holds of 1.5-11 h that begin 5-14 min AFTER a borrow returned successfully, when ha_carrier reports preset_mode=manual while hold_activity still names a preset (sometimes with the nudge's stale setpoints). URA books it as a human override (zero delta), the arrester declines, S1 locks itself out, and infinite_holds keeps it.
why: Verified in ha_carrier source: preset_mode comes from the STATUS feed (periodic poll, lags; climate.py:158-172), hold_activity from the CONFIG feed (prompt; :261), setpoints from the status-named activity (:230). The earlier 'not URA' conclusion rested on ura_activity_log, which by construction never records set_temperature — ac_ramp_events held the evidence all along.
implications: Supersedes entry 143's claim that the residual is the Bryant native-schedule reclaim, and the 09-17 diagnosis. Fix belongs in W1 (read coherence: manual counts as a person only when config hold_activity agrees; presets-only returns). Nudges stay ON (operator). Every thermostat write must be durably logged at the funnel so 'did URA write?' is one query.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a strand occurs where hold_activity == manual (a genuine hold) — then the coherence rule is insufficient.
